newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS "DON'T WANT TO PLAY IN FRONT OF FOUR CATS".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS "DON'T WANT TO PLAY IN FRONT OF FOUR CATS".

text.p: European Cup holders Juventus, who thrashed France's Paris St Germain 6-1 in a European Supercup first leg, want to play next month's home leg in Sicily instead of their native Turin.

The Turin daily newspaper Tuttosport reported that the Italian league leaders had asked UEFA for permission to play the February 5 match in Palermo's La Favorita stadium instead of the cavernous Delle Alpi ground in the northern city.
"In all probability La Favorita will be a sell-out...in
Turin, on February 5, there would have been four cats and a bone-splitting dose of dampness," the paper said.
The 37,500-seat La Favorita was packed on Wednesday night for Italy's first match under new coach Cesare Maldini.

Juventus, who fear an empty Delle Alpi with local fans in Turin staying at home since the result is seen as a foregone conclusion, could expect a full turnout in Palermo. The club, which celebrates its centenary this year, has an army of fans all over Italy with stronger support outside Turin than in the industrial city itself.
Juventus have also been in dispute with the local council who own the Delle Alpi and have threatened in the past to leave Turin and move to another Italian city.
Tuttosport said the French team, who had expected a relatively painless trip abroad, were weighing up the prospect of a more tiring journey to southern Italy.
